gaps: The spec named four default sets. There are six. The SDU-006 guard found routes/api/control.ts:96 (the control-panel GET fallback, server-side, now collapsed into the single source) and src/lib/controlPanel.ts:194 (the frontend placeholder ControlPanelState). The frontend one is browser code and cannot import lib/scheduler/defaults.ts without pulling config/env.ts server env parsing into the Vite bundle. It is allowlisted in the guard and pinned by value instead: a test asserts each of its literals still equals the corresponding server default, so drift on either side fails the suite. Removing that duplication properly needs a defaults endpoint or a generated constants file - not done, out of scope here.

The startup tick still arms its timer from STARTUP_TICK_DELAY_MS directly rather than from a nextAttemptAt return value. It is a boot delay, not a pacing decision, and AttemptReason has no vocabulary for it. Read strictly, this is the one place the acceptance criterion 'every scheduler timer is armed from a nextAttemptAt return value' is not met. Deliberate; revisit only if an operator reports the boot delay as unexplained.

decisions_locked: AttemptReason keeps the existing eight log strings (rate_limited_cooldown, post_publish_cooldown, system_maintenance, error_backoff, gap_recheck, already_running, adaptive, block_deadline_clamp) rather than the six the spec sketched. The spec's list collapses rate_limited_cooldown and post_publish_cooldown into one 'cooldown' and drops block_deadline_clamp. Those exact strings are the operational contract used to verify R1 in production and are named in the two prior handovers, so collapsing them would have destroyed the signal this session just used to open the R2 gate. 'normal' was renamed to 'adaptive' per the spec, since nothing greps for it.

Default reconciliation adopts the run.ts / presets.balanced / control.ts value for every conflicting field, against the lib/state/scheduler.ts outlier. Full per-field reasoning is in the resolution log. Net effect on this deployment: none, since all chosen values equal the live persisted values in runtime-controls.json and persisted state beats defaults regardless. Net effect on a fresh install: deliberate, most visibly targetPublishIntervalMinutes 120 -> 0 and activeHoursMultiplier 1.0 -> 0.8, so a new install paces like this one instead of roughly half as fast with the active-hours dial inert.

lib/scheduler/index.ts exports ./defaults.js before ./run.js. lib/state reads DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_CONTROLS through the scheduler barrel while run.ts reads block state back out of lib/state, which is a module cycle. Evaluating the dependency-free defaults module first makes the cycle harmless, and both back-edges are function-body uses rather than module-init reads. Importing lib/scheduler/defaults.js directly from lib/state would have avoided the cycle but added a module-boundary violation above the baseline of 42.
Jitter randomness is an injected input rather than a Math.random call inside nextAttemptAt. Omitting `random` applies no jitter, which is what lets the decision table assert exact interval values.

fields.why: 0 widens quiet hours from 3h to 6h, halving the overnight publish rate. 3 matches live and both other sets.
2.0 slows quiet hours a further 11%. 1.8 is what the observed cadence was calibrated against.
9 shortens the active window by an hour at the front.
Most consequential. 1.0 disables the active-hours speed-up entirely, making the dial inert.
3 recalibrates 2.3x more often, producing a twitchier multiplier for no observed benefit.
A literal silently ignores the documented RUN_INTERVAL_MINUTES var on first boot. Same default value either way.
Same env-discipline reason. The literal 10 had also already drifted from the env default of 15.

Behaviourally largest. 0 disables the blend; 120 pulls every adaptive interval halfway to 2 hours, roughly halving publish frequency. Live is 0. That is a rate decision for the operator, not a merge artefact.
Sets 1/2/4 agree; the presets omitted it, which is the SDU-005 totality bug. Now declared by every preset.
Declared on the default set, and deliberately excluded from presets so choosing a pacing profile cannot restart a stopped scheduler.
